text:
yusuf (ML Eng): quick heads-up 1: bringing boreal-11b into GTN candidate pipeline. ran a 3k-turn micro-slice called 'papertrail' across two quant builds (int5, int6). want a concise cost-vs-quality routing suggestion + a short ops fallback. baseline is orion-7b-int4.

emma (ML Eng): tl;dr numbers from the smoke run (median ctx ~200 tokens):
```
model           | quant | p95  | tps  | max_rps | score_mean | cost_per_1M
boreal-11b      | int6  | 430ms| 130  | 420     | 88.1       | $1.05
boreal-11b      | int5  | 390ms| 150  | 480     | 86.8       | $0.82
orion-7b        | int4  | 210ms| 300  | 1000    | 83.6       | $0.60
```
notes: score_mean = GTN utility (0-100), mixed slices incl. code, legal QA, summarization. p95 on shared canary hosts.

rachel (Data Sci): quality callouts: int5 loses ~1.3 points on code-completion accuracy and shows token-order issues on multi-step instructions; int6 is stable across slices and reduces hallucination markers on legal QA and multi-paragraph summarization. small-sample human review flagged more formatting regressions on int5.

tom (SRE): infra: int5 uses an aggressive weight packing path that ups throughput but has occasional tail jitter under noisy colocated load. int6 uses slower kernels but more deterministic tails. we can reserve a small dedicated canary pool to stabilize p99s. also watch memory OOMs if we push batch sizes too high.

li (Product): product priorities: for GTN pilot we need to prioritize correctness on legal and finance slices; latency matters but user-visible hallucination is higher priority. cost is important for scale. sounds like a classifier-driven routing could be good.

yusuf (ML Eng): proposed routing (intent-based hybrid):
- intent = transactional (short, factual Q/A, slot-filling) -> route to boreal-11b-int5 (cheaper, higher throughput)
- intent = creative / longform / legal / finance / code-gen -> route to boreal-11b-int6
- short queries <=64 tokens and low-complexity -> fallback to orion-7b-int4 to save cost (if classifier confidence < 0.6)
- runtime fallback: if int5 error_rate > 0.8% or p95 > 750ms -> redirect to int6 for that route; if int6 p99 > 1500ms or hallucination_rate doubles -> route to orion-7b-int4 until resolved

emma (ML Eng): rollout plan: 2% canary (24h) -> expand to 10% (72h) -> 25% (1 week) if metrics look stable. monitor: gt_score_delta, hallucination_rate (auto + manual), code-accuracy (BLEU/func tests), latency p95/p99, cost_per_hour. experiment flag: boreal/intent-hybrid-v1. abort criteria: gt_score_delta <= -1.0 overall or hallucination_rate x2 on any critical slice.

deploy-bot: deploy created: https://deploys.redwood.ai/ops/22789 (canary 2% -> boreal/intent-hybrid-v1) :rocket:

rachel (Data Sci): I'll add the three priority slices on GTN dashboard: legal-contracts, invoice-extraction, multi-turn-summaries, plus a code-correctness harness. will push example prompts to /evals/papertrail and schedule a 12h dedicated stability run for p99.

yusuf (ML Eng): perfect. ops note for runbook: classifier model should be lightweight (tiny intent model) with a confidence threshold; log reroutes and user-visible degradation reasons. short rollback blurb for support: "We've reverted a model update to restore expected formatting and accuracy. We're working on a fix and will update shortly."

emma (ML Eng): adding INF ticket for dedicated canary pool and SRE tuning. will post canary metrics in this thread at +24h and +72h.

yusuf (ML Eng): thanks everyone 1. will follow up with the first 24h snapshot here. :eyes:
